title: Committee of Supply – Head W (Ministry of Transport)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head W (Ministry of Transport)

sections.label: Transport spending and expansion plans
sections.summary: Estimated MOT expenditure for 2016 is $10.1 billion, about five times more than 10 years ago, with new terminals, seaport capacity and MRT stations coming.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Minister Heng Swee Keat had said in his Budget Statement that our estimated expenditure for MOT in 2016, at $10.1 billion, is approximately five times more than what it was 10 years ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Changi Airport Terminal 4 and Jewel Changi Airport are on track to commence operations soon.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Pasir Panjang Terminal Phases 3 and 4 will grow our seaport capacity by more than 40%, come end-2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: There will be an MRT extension or new line open almost every year for the next five years, adding 30 more stations to our MRT network.

sections.label: Priority queues for vulnerable commuters
sections.summary: The speaker cites the need for transport accessible to all Singaporeans and welcomes LTA's plans for priority queues for the elderly and disabled.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: I raise the example to show that a truly efficient and effective transportation model must be convenient and accessible to all Singaporeans and not just the able-bodied majority.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: I therefore read with great pleasure LTA's recent plans to introduce priority queues for the elderly, disabled and others at MRT stations and bus interchanges.

sections.label: Upgrading older MRT stations
sections.summary: Older MRT stations like Khatib look worn out, and plans exist to upgrade 17 stations by 2018, including Khatib.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: By contrast, older MRT stations like Khatib are comparatively shabby and look worn out after years of heavy usage by an increasing number of commuters.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am pleased to note that there are plans to upgrade 17 stations by 2018 and to find Khatib among the list.

sections.label: MRT disruption incidents and delays
sections.summary: In the past 13 months at least 50 MRT disruptions were reported, almost half exceeding 30 minutes, with 14 major disruptions last year, up from 10.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In the past 13 months, we have seen at least 50 incidents of MRT disruptions reported and almost half of such delays exceeded 30 minutes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: There were 14 major MRT disruptions last year, up from 10.

sections.label: Fatal accident near Pasir Ris station
sections.summary: On 22 March this year, two MRT maintenance staff were hit by a train near Pasir Ris MRT station and suffered fatal injuries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Chairman, on 22 March this year, two MRT maintenance staff were hit by a train near Pasir Ris MRT station and suffered fatal injuries.

sections.label: Review of train maintenance work
sections.summary: MOT should comprehensively review how train operators carry out maintenance so such incidents never happen again, after two SMRT staff were killed on 22 March.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: MOT should take a comprehensive review of how our train operators carry out their maintenance work to ensure that such unfortunate incidents should never again happen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, on 22 March this year, two SMRT staff were killed when an MRT train collided into them while they were on the tracks assisting with repair work.

sections.label: SMRT track maintenance safety measures
sections.summary: LTA and MOM required SMRT to adopt five measures for maintenance during train service hours from 31 March.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: Later that day, LTA and the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) issued a press release requiring SMRT to carry out the following measures if maintenance work are carried out during train service hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: This is to take effect from 31 March: (a) train running on sections of the track where personnel are working on must operate on manual, not automatic mode; (b) trains to cease operating on the relevant section of the track before repair personnel is allowed on it; (c) robust authentication between personnel on track and the operations control centre to verify track isolation; (d) measures for isolation to be in place until staff have left the work area and track site; and finally, (e) watchman to be deployed to alert personnel of incoming trains.

sections.label: Electric bus battery range and lifespan
sections.summary: Electric bus batteries can power buses up to 250 kilometres per charge and last about seven-and-a-half years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Electric bus batteries can now power buses to travel longer with claimed ranges of 250 kilometres on a single four- to five-hour charge, which should be sufficient in most cases to operate for a full day without the need to recharge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The batteries themselves have also longer lifespans and are estimated to last about seven-and-a-half years with more than 4,000 recharging cycles in a lifespan.

sections.label: NTWU Executive Secretary interest declaration
sections.summary: The speaker declared an interest as Executive Secretary of the National Transport Workers' Union.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Chairman, I would like to declare my interest as the Executive Secretary of the National Transport Workers' Union (NTWU).

sections.label: Bus captain hiring and wages
sections.summary: Public bus operators seek over 3,000 bus captains this year, and starting wages rose over 30% since 2012.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In fact, this year alone, the public bus operators seek to hire more than 3,000 bus captains.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Although the starting wages of the bus captains have increased by over 30% since 2012, more needs to be done to enhance the bus captain profession to attract more Singaporeans to join the trade as well as to retain the current crop of bus captains.

sections.label: Bus captains health screening results
sections.summary: A union health screening of close to 900 bus captains found eight in 10 had unhealthy BMI, blood pressure or cholesterol.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Through a recent health screening project piloted by the union involving close to 900 bus captains, we found that eight out of 10 had unhealthy BMI, blood pressure or cholesterol.

sections.label: Proposed annual Bus Captains' Day
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Ministry will consider designating a yearly Bus Captains' Day to recognise their contributions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Our bus captains deserve greater recognition than what they receive today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I hope that the Ministry can consider designating a "Bus Captains' Day" every year to recognise their dedicated contributions and service to our community.

sections.label: SMRT investigations and reviews
sections.summary: SMRT's internal investigation is done and reviewed by independent experts, while LTA, Police and MOM investigations are ongoing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: SMRT has completed its internal investigation and its findings are being reviewed by independent experts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) is conducting its own investigation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Statutory investigations by the Police and the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) are ongoing.

sections.label: Interim safety orders and committee
sections.summary: MOM issued interim safety orders to SMRT and SMRT set up a safety review committee with international experts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: But rail operations and maintenance have to go on.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: So, even as investigations are ongoing, MOM, in consultation with LTA, found it prudent to issue interim safety orders to SMRT to ensure the safety of railway workers and commuters.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: In addition, SMRT has set up a safety review committee with experts drawn from international transport operators.

sections.label: MRT train-kilometres between delays
sections.summary: Trains averaged 133,000 train-kilometres between delays over five minutes, below Hong Kong's 300,000 but up about 40% from 2014.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Last year, trains on the MRT network travelled an average of 133,000 train-kilometres between delays of more than five minutes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: The figure of 133,000 kilometres is way below Hong Kong Mass Transit Railway's MKBF of 300,000 kilometres.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: But it is a significant improvement of about 40% from 2014 of 93,000 kilometres.

sections.label: MRT disruptions over 30 minutes
sections.summary: The MRT experienced disruptions exceeding 30 minutes on 14 occasions last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Yes, our MRT did experience disruptions exceeding 30 minutes, on 14 occasions last year.

sections.label: Downtown Line continuous service days
sections.summary: The Downtown Line has crossed 171 days of continuous service without any major disruption.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: The Downtown Line (DTL) has crossed 171 days of continuous service without any major disruption; 171 days, almost half a year, without any major incident.

sections.label: Hardware replacement and upgrading investment
sections.summary: About a billion dollars is being invested in hardware replacement and upgrading.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Second, we are investing about a billion dollars in hardware replacement and upgrading.

sections.label: Chartered Rail Engineers Scheme and Academy
sections.summary: The Singapore Rail Academy is being set up to work with rail operators and Institutes of Higher Learning on training, accreditation and certification.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: I am glad to see the Chartered Rail Engineers Scheme gaining momentum.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: We are setting up the Singapore Rail Academy to quicken this process.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: The Academy will work with the rail operators and the Institutes of Higher Learning to deepen rail engineering capabilities through training, as well as for accreditation and certification of training programmes and competencies.

sections.label: Adding trains and extending rail lines
sections.summary: New trains are being added to all lines, headways shortened, and several lines extended while new lines are built and planned.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: But we also have to address peak period crowding and improve connectivity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: That is why we are, in parallel, adding new trains to all lines, shortening headways on NSL and EWL, extending EWL westward, DTL eastward, NEL northward, not to mention building the new Thomson-East Coast Line, while planning the new Jurong Region Line and Cross-Island Line.

sections.label: Changing NSL and EWL signalling
sections.summary: The signalling system of the NSL and EWL will be changed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Third, we will be changing the signalling system of the NSL and EWL.

sections.label: Rail network investment
sections.summary: More than $30 billion was invested in the rail network over the last 15 years, with more investment planned for the next 15.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: The rail network is the backbone of our public transport system.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: We have invested more than $30 billion over the last 15 years and we will be investing even more in the next 15.

sections.label: Bus Service Enhancement Programme buses
sections.summary: Under the Bus Service Enhancement Programme, 800 buses have been added and another 200 will be added by the end of next year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Under the Bus Service Enhancement Programme (BSEP), we have added 800 buses, and will add another 200 by the end of next year.

sections.label: Self-driving technology readiness
sections.summary: Self-driving technology is not yet ready for mass deployment and may be 10 to 15 years away, depending on public acceptance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Self-driving technology is not yet ready for mass deployment and may be 10 to 15 years away, depending on the pace of public acceptance.

sections.label: Public transport investment priority
sections.summary: The passage states incumbents need help to cope with changes, so public transport investments were given top priority and private transport second place.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: That is why we need to help incumbents prepare to cope with these changes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Therefore, we decided to give top priority to investments in public transport and to put private transport in second place.

sections.label: Bus Carnival attendance
sections.summary: The recent Bus Carnival was attended by 140,000 Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: The recent Bus Carnival was attended by 140,000 Singaporeans.

sections.label: Car-lite Singapore public transport
sections.summary: To promote a car-lite Singapore, the Government should provide better public transport so residents can travel to office and back without driving.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: To promote a car-lite Singapore, the Government should provide better public transport for residents so that they can get to office and back home without the need to drive.

sections.label: Shuttle buses from MRT stations
sections.summary: The passage asks whether LTA would consider running peak-hour shuttle buses from MRT stations to and from private estates under the new bus model system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: With the new bus model system, would LTA consider running shuttle buses during peak hours from MRT stations to and from the private estates?

sections.label: Elderly-friendly roads and amenities
sections.summary: As elderly citizens increase, LTA should design public roads and amenities for elderly travel, with more lifts at pedestrian overhead bridges and signalised crossings where lifts are not feasible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: As there are more and more elderly citizens, LTA should design the public roads and supporting amenities to facilitate travel for these elderly residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: There should be more lifts for pedestrian overhead bridges, and where such lifts are not feasible, signalised crossing should be provided.

sections.label: Lift or signalised crossing appeal
sections.summary: The passage states a ramp is unused by elderly because it is too long, making it a white elephant, and appeals to MOT and LTA to reconsider a lift or signalised traffic crossing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: Although there is a ramp, none of the elderly wants to use it because it is too long a distance to climb and, hence, has become a white elephant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: Hence, I appeal to the compassion of MOT and LTA officers to reconsider having a lift at the pedestrian overhead bridge or, alternatively, to consider a signalised traffic crossing.

sections.label: Lifts per path capacity
sections.summary: Each path currently has at most one lift, typically small and fitting up to two wheeled mobility devices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Currently, there is at most one lift per path.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: These lifts are typically small and accommodate up to two wheeled mobility devices.

sections.label: Wheelchair taxi fares
sections.summary: SMRT, Comfort and other firms provide some wheelchair-capable taxis, but fares are generally at least $50 per trip.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: SMRT, Comfort and other firms now provide some taxis that can ferry wheelchairs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, the fare they charge is generally at least $50 per trip.

sections.label: Wheelchair restraint safety standard
sections.summary: Safety of wheelchair users and other passengers is not ensured, and a worldwide standard called WTORS exists.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This will not ensure the safety of both the wheelchair user and, other passengers who might be injured by a flying wheelchair, so to speak, should an accident occur.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: There is a worldwide standard known as the Wheelchair Tie-Down and Occupant Restraint System (WTORS).

sections.label: Hospitals without covered walkways
sections.summary: Simei MRT station is about 500 metres from Changi General Hospital with no covered walkway, as at Khoo Teck Puat Hospital.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Simei MRT station is only about 500 metres away from the Changi General Hospital but there is no covered walkway linking the two.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: This is also the case at Khoo Teck Puat Hospital, which is about 800 metres away from Yishun MRT station on a straight line basis.

sections.label: 2030 public transport targets
sections.summary: By 2030, an MRT station will be within a five-minute walk in the central area and eight in 10 households within 10 minutes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: By 2030, there will be an MRT station within a five-minute walk from any location in the central area and eight in 10 households will be within a 10-minute walk of a station.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: By then, three out of four commuters will travel by public transport daily.

sections.label: Walk2Ride linkway initiative
sections.summary: In 2013, MOT announced the Walk2Ride initiative to build 200 kilometres worth of linkways throughout the island.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: For instance, in 2013, MOT announced the "Walk2Ride" initiative to build 200 Page: 16 kilometres worth of linkways throughout the island.

sections.label: AMAP footpath recommendations
sections.summary: AMAP recommended to the Ministry that cyclists and PMD users be allowed on footpaths.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: In its recommendations to the Ministry last month, AMAP recommended that cyclists and users of personal mobility devices (PMDs) be allowed on footpaths.

sections.label: Pedestrian safety and speed limits
sections.summary: The speaker asks how the Ministry will enforce the Panel's recommended speed limits and says pedestrians should not be put at risk.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Pedestrians, especially the elderly and young children, should not be put at risk for the convenience of cyclists and users of PMDs.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: I would also like to ask the Ministry how it intends to enforce speed limits, which the Panel recommended at 15 kilometres per hour on footpaths and 25 	kilometres per hour on cycling and shared paths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It recommended that bicycles and PMDs should be allowed on footpaths.

sections.label: E-bike weight speed width
sections.summary: The speaker agrees with the Panel's recommendations on e-bike maximum weight of 20 kilograms, maximum speed of 25 kilometres per hour and width.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: On electric bicycles (e-bikes), I agree with the Panel's recommendations regarding maximum weight of 20 kilograms, maximum speed of 25 	kilometres per hour and the devices' width.

sections.label: Authorised e-bike sales and registration
sections.summary: The speaker asks if only authorised e-bikes may be sold and suggests owners of existing unauthorised e-bikes be allowed to apply for authorisation and registration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry consider only allowing authorised e-bikes to be sold in Singapore?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In respect of the existing unauthorised e-bikes which may technically comply with the new proposed rules, may I suggest that the Ministry consider, at least on a one-off basis, to allow owners of such e-bikes to apply directly for authorisation and registration?

sections.label: Separate paths for bicycles
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Ministry to reconsider building separate dedicated paths for bicycles, citing risks to vulnerable pedestrians and residents' feedback.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Vulnerable pedestrians, such as the elderly and young children, will face a higher risk from cyclists once they start sharing footpaths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I urge the Ministry to reconsider building separate dedicated paths for bicycles − in Mandarin − "请三思".

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I rise to make the same call in light of the recommendations of AMAP and the frequency of feedback from residents, especially elderly residents, about accidents and near-accidents between cyclists and pedestrians on footpaths, zebra crossings and pedestrian crossings and even bus stops.

sections.label: Cyclists dismounting at bus stops
sections.summary: The speaker believes cyclists using footpaths, pedestrian crossings or near bus stops must dismount and walk across these areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Members may also have had residents complaining about cyclists who zipped by just as they were disembarking from buses at bus stops.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I believe it must be compulsory for cyclists who use footpaths and pedestrian crossings or who are near bus stops to dismount from their bicycles and walk across these areas which are more prone to accidents and heavy pedestrian traffic.

sections.label: Dismount-and-push rule for cyclists
sections.summary: The passage says a dismount-and-push rule for cyclists at critical areas should be implemented and enforced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Likewise, we should implement a dismount-and-push rule for cyclists at critical areas and enforce it.

sections.label: Higher fine for non-compliant e-bikes
sections.summary: The passage proposes increasing the fine for first-time offenders using or selling non-compliant e-bikes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Consequently, it is proposed that we increase the fine for first-time offenders using or selling non-compliant e-bikes.

sections.label: Non-compliant e-bike offences rise
sections.summary: The passage states offences involving non-compliant e-bikes rose significantly to over 1,000 notices in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The number of offences involving the use of non-compliant e-bikes has increased significantly to over 1,000 notices in 2015.

sections.label: MOT rail network expansion plans
sections.summary: The passage states MOT plans to double the rail network and add over 100 new MRT stations in 15 years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Members of the House would already be aware of MOT's plans to double our rail network and add more than 100 new MRT stations across the island in the next 15 years.

sections.label: Residents near train stations by 2030
sections.summary: The passage states that by 2030, eight in 10 residents will be within a 10-minute walk of a train station.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: By 2030, eight in 10 residents all over Singapore will be within a 10-minute walk of a train station.

sections.label: Funding for commuter improvements
sections.summary: The passage states the Government committed nearly $1 billion in the last five years to improve FLMC for commuters.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In the last five years, the Government has committed nearly $1 billion to improve FLMC for commuters.

sections.label: Sheltered walkways to MRT stations
sections.summary: By 2018, every MRT and LRT station will be connected by sheltered walkways to nearby schools, healthcare facilities and public amenities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: By 2018, every MRT and LRT station will be connected by sheltered walkways to nearby schools, healthcare facilities and public amenities.

sections.label: Changi hospital walkway completion
sections.summary: The planned walkway from Changi General Hospital to Simei MRT station will be completed by 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The planned walkway from Changi General Hospital to Simei MRT station will be completed by 2017.

sections.label: Barrier-free access at transport nodes
sections.summary: All MRT stations and bus interchanges offer barrier-free access today, and almost all bus stops and buses are barrier-free as well.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Today, all MRT stations and bus interchanges offer barrier-free access.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Almost all bus stops and buses are barrier-free as well.

sections.label: Lifts at overhead bridges
sections.summary: LTA is installing lifts at 41 overhead bridges near places frequented by the elderly or disabled, and will expand this to about 50 more bridges.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: LTA is currently installing lifts at 41 overhead bridges, prioritising the bridges near places frequented by the elderly or disabled.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This includes transport hubs, healthcare institutions, welfare homes, homes for the aged and schools for special needs children.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We will expand this programme to about 50 more bridges.

sections.label: Cycling networks in more towns
sections.summary: Residents in Tampines, Sembawang, Pasir Ris, Changi-Simei and Yishun enjoy completed networks, and cycling networks will be built in 11 more towns over five years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Today, residents in Tampines, Sembawang, Pasir Ris, Changi-Simei and Yishun are already enjoying their completed networks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We will build cycling networks in 11 more towns over the next five years.

sections.label: Government accepts Panel recommendations
sections.summary: The Government will accept the Panel's recommendations in full.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: So, think thrice but, after that, take action.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: I am pleased to share that the Government will accept the Panel's recommendations in full.

sections.label: Bicycles and PMDs on paths
sections.summary: New rules allow bicycles and PMDs on footpaths, shared paths and cycling paths, but not power-assisted bicycles on footpaths.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: These new rules will mean that bicycles and PMDs like kick-scooters, e-scooters, electric unicycles and hoverboards, can be used on footpaths, shared paths and cycling paths.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We will, however, not allow power-assisted bicycles or e-bikes, on footpaths, because their nature and use tend to pose a higher safety risk to other path users.

sections.label: Active Mobility awareness campaign
sections.summary: A nationwide Active Mobility campaign launches this April to raise awareness about proposed policies, rules and code of conduct.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The first thing we will do is to launch a nationwide Active Mobility campaign this April to raise awareness about the proposed policies, rules and code of conduct.

sections.label: Programme rollout in schools
sections.summary: The programme launches in May and will be progressively rolled out in schools, community centres and foreign worker dormitories.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The programme will be launched in May and will be progressively rolled out in schools, community centres and foreign worker dormitories.

sections.label: LTA enforcement team
sections.summary: LTA will set up a dedicated enforcement team and join Traffic Police on joint enforcement exercises at hotspots.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: LTA will set up a dedicated enforcement team and will join the Traffic Police on joint enforcement exercises at hotspots.

sections.label: Illegally modified e-bikes
sections.summary: Irresponsible users illegally modify e-bikes to travel at high speeds, posing a safety hazard, and a grace period for registration is accepted.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Some irresponsible users have illegally modified their e-bikes to travel at high speeds of 40	kilometres per hour, even 70 	kilometres per hour on the roads, effectively making them similar to motorcycles.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: They pose a safety hazard to pedestrians and motorists and, if I may add, to themselves.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We accept that there should be a grace period for e-bike owners to register and will need more time to work out the details.

sections.label: Enforcement against errant retailers
sections.summary: LTA has stepped up enforcement against errant retailers and will amend legislation to tighten up on the sale of non-compliant e-bikes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Since last year, LTA has stepped up enforcement against errant retailers and will continue to do so.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We will also amend legislation to tighten up on the sale of non-compliant e-bikes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: LTA will study this as we go about, together with implementation of e-bike registration.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We target to implement most of the changes by the end of this year.

sections.label: Tokyo versus Singapore walking cycling
sections.summary: Thirty-seven percent of Tokyo trips are made on foot or by bicycle, compared to 17% in Singapore today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Thirty-seven Page: 26 percent of all trips in Tokyo are made on foot or on bicycles, compared to just 17% in Singapore today.

sections.label: Cat B COE quota share
sections.summary: Cat B COE was 10% of the total COE quota in January 2000 and 28% in January 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: In January 2000, Cat B COE only constituted 10% of the total COE quota for that month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: In January 2016, Cat B COE constituted 28% of the total COE quota.

sections.label: Surcharge for additional household cars
sections.summary: A Member asks whether a COE surcharge could be added for cars beyond the first or second in a household.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This will become a cat-and-mouse game between the recategorisation of Cat A and the re-engineering of luxury makes to fit Cat A, especially in car-lite Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, for a fairer COE system, would the Government consider adding a surcharge to the COE for cars owned by a single-generation household beyond the first car and a multigeneration household beyond the second car?

sections.label: Class 2B motorcycle and Cat D COE
sections.summary: A class 2B motorcycle costs about $11,000, with Cat D COE averaging $6,106 in 2015, three times the 2011 average of $2,098.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Presently, a class 2B motorcycle will cost an average of $11,000, with the Category D or Cat D COE costing an average of $6,106 in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is three times higher compared to the average in 2011 which was $2,098.

sections.label: Motorcycle COE prices since 2014
sections.summary: Motorcycle COE prices have risen significantly since 2014, while car COE prices have largely stayed the same.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Motorcycle COE prices have increased significantly since 2014, even though our COEs for cars have largely stayed the same in terms of pricing.

sections.label: Cat C COE higher than Cat B
sections.summary: In February and March first bidding, Cat C COE prices were higher than Cat B, mainly because the Early Turnover Scheme reduces the Cat C quota.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In fact, for the first bidding in February and March this year, we have a perverse situation where the price of Cat C COEs is higher than Cat B COEs for bigger passenger cars.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The main reason for the high cost of Cat C COEs is that the quota set aside for Cat C is reduced by the number of vehicles registered under the Early Turnover Scheme, which encourages commercial vehicle owners to switch to cleaner models.

sections.label: Cat C COE quota reduction
sections.summary: Cat C COEs available for bidding fall to less than 1,000 for the quarter because Early Turnover Scheme COEs are deducted from the quota.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For the current quarter, there should have been more than 4,000 Cat C COEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, as 90% of the COEs used under the Early Turnover Scheme are deducted from the Cat C quota and there are more than 3,000 vehicles registered under this scheme, the number of Cat C COEs available for bidding is substantially reduced to less than 1,000 for the quarter; or about 300 per month.

sections.label: Review of commercial vehicle COEs
sections.summary: The speaker urges MOT to comprehensively review how COEs for commercial vehicles are determined.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: To help businesses and for the reasons mentioned, I urge MOT to do a comprehensive review of the way COEs for commercial vehicles are determined.

sections.label: Taxi customer satisfaction survey
sections.summary: Over the past three years, more than 90% of annual Taxi Customer Satisfaction Survey respondents say they are satisfied with taxi services.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: For the past three years, in our annual Taxi Customer Satisfaction Survey, more than 90% of respondents say that they are satisfied with taxi services.

sections.label: Increase in pre-booked taxi trips
sections.summary: Pre-booked taxi trips rose by 50% over three years, mostly from app bookings.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: The number of pre-booked taxi trips has increased by 50% over the last three years, with the bulk of this increase coming from bookings via apps.

sections.label: Shortened TDVL and refresher exemptions
sections.summary: LTA is asked to shorten the TDVL course and exempt good drivers with no demerit points from mandated refresher courses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: In addition, we can deliver more training online, rather than in the classroom.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: I have, therefore, asked LTA to shorten the TDVL course with appropriate modifications.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: I have also asked LTA to exempt good drivers who do not have any demerit points from having to attend mandated refresher courses.

sections.label: Private Hire Car Driver Vocational Licensing
sections.summary: With app growth, LTA will introduce a Private Hire Car Driver Vocational Licensing framework to ensure commuter safety.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, with the growth of apps like Uber and GrabCar, some basic regulations are needed to ensure that the commuters' interests, particularly safety, are taken care of.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Hence, LTA will introduce a new Private Hire Car Driver Vocational Licensing framework (PDVL).

sections.label: Taxi to dual licence conversion
sections.summary: Applicants need two years' driving experience, and taxi drivers can convert their TDVL to a dual TDVL-PDVL licence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: For the safety of commuters, applicants for the licence must have a minimum driving experience of two years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: We recognise that the TDVL curriculum covers a substantial part of the PDVL curriculum.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Hence, we will make it easy for taxi drivers to convert their TDVL to a dual TDVL-PDVL licence.

sections.label: Private hire car registration decals
sections.summary: Private hire cars providing chauffeured services must register with LTA and display a distinctive, tamper-evident exterior decal.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: In order to strengthen enforcement against errant drivers, private hire cars providing chauffeured services will have to be registered with LTA and they will display a distinctive, tamper-evident decal that will be visible from the car's exterior.

sections.label: System development and 2020 implementation
sections.summary: LTA announced the system is being developed and will be implemented from 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: As LTA had announced, the system is being developed and will be implemented from 2020.

sections.label: Motorcycle short-term renewals and quota
sections.summary: Repeated short-term renewals for motorcycles favour incumbent owners, delay deregistration and reduce the quota for new buyers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Allowing repeated short-term renewals for motorcycles, however attractive, favours the incumbent owners and delays timely deregistration, and this reduces the quota for potential new buyers of motorcycles.

sections.label: Public consultation on surcharge proposal
sections.summary: MOT consulted the public in 2013, and the outcome was that this surcharge or Assoc Prof Daniel Goh's proposal would be easy to circumvent.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: MOT has consulted the public extensively in 2013 on this issue and the outcome of the discussion was that this form of surcharge or the form of proposal given by Assoc Prof Daniel Goh would be very easy to circumvent.

sections.label: Cat E COE contribution rate
sections.summary: To maintain a more stable COE supply, the Cat E contribution rate was lowered from 25% to 20%, 15% and 10%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, to maintain a more stable supply of COEs in each category, we had lowered the Cat E contribution rate from 25% previously to 20% back in 2012 and further to 15% in 2013 and to 10% in February last year.

sections.label: Early Turnover Scheme Cat C impact
sections.summary: The Early Turnover Scheme reduces the Cat C quota for bidding but also reduces actual demand for new Cat C COEs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: On the impact of the Early Turnover Scheme (ETS) on Cat C quotas and premiums, while the ETS reduces the quota available for bidding, it also reduces the actual demand for new Cat C COEs.

sections.label: Cat C COE price trend
sections.summary: Cat C COE prices have shown a slight downward trend generally since the Early Turnover Scheme began in April 2013.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: In fact, what we have observed is that Cat C COE prices have seen a slight downward trend generally since the introduction of the ETS in April 2013.

sections.label: More car owners renewing COEs
sections.summary: More car owners renewing their COEs has tempered previously expected increases in Cats A and B COE supply by over 10% in the last two quarters.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Recently, many more car owners have decided to renew their COEs and this has tempered the previously expected increases in Cats A and B COE supply by more than 10% in the last two quarters.

sections.label: Air and maritime hub capacity
sections.summary: Government announcements to build Terminal 5, a third Changi runway and a new Tuas port are designed to build air and maritime hub capacity in Southeast Asia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In line with this, the Government's announcements to build Page: 34 Terminal 5, a third runway at Changi Airport, as well as a new port in Tuas, are designed to build our capacity as an air and maritime hub in Southeast Asia.

sections.label: NOL sale and container volumes
sections.summary: The question asks about MOT's plans to ensure container volumes are not lost and the logistics sector is not adversely impacted by the NOL sale.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: With the sale of NOL, what are some of MOT's plans to ensure that we do not lose container volumes and that the sale would not adversely impact our logistics sector, in particular, in the mid to long term, where the new entity's private sector interest may change due to competitive or business priorities?

sections.label: Jobs from new hubs
sections.summary: The question asks about expected new jobs and business opportunities from these hubs and the Ministry's manpower plans for a Singaporean Core.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: What are the expected new jobs and business opportunities that these hubs will bring to Singapore and what are the Ministry's manpower development plans to provide these enhanced sectors with a Singaporean Core?

sections.label: Budget airline crew stress
sections.summary: An advisor to an airline house union understands low-cost carrier operating modes can cause high stress and fatigue among flight crew.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
sentences.text: Through interactions with the budget airline staff in my capacity as an advisor to one of the airline house unions, I understand that the operating mode of low-cost carriers can potentially generate high levels of stress and fatigue among the flight crew.

sections.label: Study of airline crew stress
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Ministry will study the needs, challenges and stress of budget and full-service airline crew, sectors contributing 13% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
sentences.text: Will the Ministry consider embarking on a study to understand the needs, challenges and stress faced by the crew in budget airlines, as well as full-service airlines?

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Together, the direct economic contribution of these two sectors amounts to 13% of our GDP.

sections.label: Changi passenger record 2015
sections.summary: A record 55.4 million passengers passed through Changi in 2015, helped by rebounding tourist arrivals from China, Thailand and Australia.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Thanks in part to a rebound in tourist arrivals from key markets, such as China, Thailand and Australia, a record 55.4 million passengers flowed through Changi in 2015.

sections.label: Terminal 4 and Jewel openings
sections.summary: Terminal 4 is on track to open in the second half of 2017 and Jewel Changi Airport in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Terminal 4 is on track to open in the second half of 2017 and Jewel Changi Airport in 2019.

sections.label: Terminal 5 opening and upgrade
sections.summary: Terminal 5 will open in the late 2020s and be operational until about 2050 before a major upgrade is due.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Terminal 5 will open in the late 2020s and be operational till about 2050 before a major upgrade is due.

sections.label: Singapore FIR flight numbers
sections.summary: Last year it handled about 650,000 flights, 50% more than 10 years ago, managed by the Singapore FIR.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Last year, it handled some 650,000 flights, which are 50% more than 10 years ago.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Six hundred and fifty thousand flights that our Singapore FIR manages, flying through our skies.

sections.label: Projected Singapore FIR flights
sections.summary: By 2025, more than a million flights are projected to fly through the Singapore FIR annually.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: By 2025, it is projected that more than a million flights will fly through the Singapore FIR annually.

sections.label: Air traffic controller pool growth
sections.summary: The pool of air traffic controllers has expanded and will grow from 380 today to 600 within five years.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: For example, our pool of air traffic controllers has expanded and will grow further from 380 today to 600 within the next five years.

sections.label: CAAS ATM research funding
sections.summary: CAAS is commissioning research and development in ATM and has set aside $200 million to develop Singapore as a Centre of Excellence for ATM.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: With a firm eye on the future, CAAS is commissioning significant research and development efforts in ATM.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: It has embarked on an initiative to develop Singapore as a Centre of Excellence for ATM by setting aside $200 million to fund research and development projects.

sections.label: ASEAN Seamless ASEAN Sky call
sections.summary: ASEAN Leaders called last year for the implementation of a Seamless ASEAN Sky, to capture aviation connectivity opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If we cannot do so, we will fail to capture the opportunities that aviation connectivity provides to all our economies.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: It was, therefore, far-sighted that ASEAN Leaders called for the implementation of a Seamless ASEAN Sky when they met last year.

sections.label: Maritime sector employment levels
sections.summary: Employment levels in the maritime sector have remained stable at around 170,000.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Employment levels in the maritime sector have also remained stable at around 170,000.

sections.label: Shipping concessions annual savings
sections.summary: Together with existing concessions, the full slate of concessions is expected to yield $18 million in annual savings for shipping companies.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Taken together with existing concessions, the full slate of concessions is expected to yield $18 million in annual savings for shipping companies.

sections.label: Maritime Singapore shipping groups
sections.summary: Maritime Singapore hosts over 130 international shipping groups and more than 5,000 maritime establishments.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Today, Maritime Singapore is home to over 130 international shipping groups and more than 5,000 maritime establishments.

sections.label: CMA-CGM NOL acquisition proposal
sections.summary: CMA-CGM intends to establish its regional head office in Singapore and commit more volumes through Singapore in its proposal to acquire NOL.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In its proposal to acquire NOL, CMA-CGM has made it clear its intention to establish its regional head office in Singapore and commit more volumes through Singapore.

sections.label: Funding for research organisations
sections.summary: A total of $150 million has been set aside to support numerous research organisations and projects.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: A total of $150 million has been set aside to support numerous research organisations and projects.

sections.label: MINT Fund top-up extension
sections.summary: MPA will top up the MINT Fund by a further $50 million and extend its term to 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If the concept works, it will mean lower cost for ship owners to meet the higher standards for clean energy use that they must comply with in the future.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I am pleased to announce that MPA will top up the MINT Fund by a further $50 million and extend its term to 2021.

sections.label: Internship Reimbursement Scheme rollout
sections.summary: MPA will roll out the Internship Reimbursement Scheme to help students gain relevant work experience.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: MPA will roll out the Internship Reimbursement Scheme to help students gain relevant work experience.

sections.label: Graduates Attachment Programme reintroduction
sections.summary: MPA will reintroduce the Graduates Attachment Programme, or GAP, for those fresh out of school.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: For those fresh out of school, MPA will reintroduce the Graduates Attachment Programme or GAP in short.

sections.label: Maritime Career Conversion Scheme support
sections.summary: The Maritime Career Conversion Scheme subsidises training costs and provides wage support for Singaporeans switching to the maritime sector.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: For Singaporeans looking to make a career switch into the maritime sector, the Maritime Career Conversion Scheme will subsidise training costs and provide wage support.

sections.label: MPA manpower initiatives funding
sections.summary: MPA will set aside $12 million for enhanced manpower initiatives expected to benefit some 5,000 Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: All in all, MPA will set aside $12 million for its enhanced manpower initiatives which are expected to benefit some 5,000 Singaporeans.

sections.label: COE mechanism and market decision
sections.summary: The current COE mechanism is the best available, and Cat E COEs moved to Cat B reflect the market's decision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: Ultimately, even though there are imperfections, the current COE mechanism is the best that we have today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: As the Member rightly pointed out, where Cat E COEs have been moved to Cat B, that is the market's decision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: If we come back to the fundamental reasons for this allocation, well, I will keep the answer short as well − let the market decide.

sections.label: Metro work area safety principle
sections.summary: The general safety principle for metros is isolating the work area from passing trains, or manual slow-speed operation if a train passes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: The general safety principle that governs all metros, including SMRT, is that one must isolate the work area/space from any passing train.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: It does not mean the train cannot pass through the work area but, if it does, then the train has to be manually operated and at slow speed.

sections.label: Taxi service standards review
sections.summary: The quality of service standards and taxi availability framework is undergoing review and will be consistently reviewed for relevance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: The quality of service standards and the taxi availability framework is currently undergoing review and would be consistently reviewed to make sure that it is updated and relevant to the evolving market and industry landscape.

sections.label: ERP 2.0 charging model objective
sections.summary: It is too early to say on the charging model; ERP 2.0's primary objective is congestion management, not raising revenue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: On the charging model that Mr Perera had asked about, it is too early to say.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: The primary objective of ERP 2.0 is for congestion management; it has never been to raise revenue.

sections.label: Motorcycle engine power COE categories
sections.summary: 70% of motorcycles are below 200cc and 30% above 200cc, but splitting COEs into smaller categories would add rigidity and higher COE price volatility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: In terms of the engine power, 70% of the motorcycle population are motorcycles below 200cc, and about 30% are those above 200cc.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: But if we were to split the COEs into smaller categories, it will bring in rigidity and the subsequent effect will lead to higher volatility of COE prices for motorcycles.
